review.notes: Drafted for #5. time.start is D-Day, when the strongpoint was fought over. Wikipedia's Omaha Beach passages used here cite Badsey & Bean, Omaha Beach (Sutton, 2004), pp. 42, 71, 76-77, and Omaha Beachhead (Historical Division, 1945), pp. 63-65 (ch. 4). Neither could be read from this session (history.army.mil returns 403, web.archive.org is not reachable), so the cites point at Wikipedia; a checker should replace them with Omaha Beachhead page cites (source cmh-omaha-beachhead) once it is readable. That surviving concrete remains are present is taken from Wikidata only (instance of bunker, made of reinforced concrete, has part Regelbau 699 and tobruk), so it stays unreviewed. Coordinate is Wikidata P625, given to 4 decimals only (about 10 m), so accuracy is approximate; OSM node id from Wikidata P11693, not checked against OSM directly. Heinrich Severloh's ammunition claims are left out on purpose: Wikipedia itself says they are disputed, and no source for either side was readable.

summary.text: German strongpoint (Widerstandsnest, 'resistance nest') on the bluffs at Colleville-sur-Mer, covering the E-3 draw. It was one of 15 strongpoints along Omaha Beach, numbered WN-60 in the east to WN-74 in the west. On D-Day American troops got inside its wire early in the assault, and by mid-morning only one machine gun was reported still firing from it. Wikidata records surviving reinforced-concrete bunkers at the site.
